summary: One method, Tick(deltaTime), so UpdateManager can drive an object instead of Unity calling Update.
purpose: The contract UpdateManager drives. It exists so a central loop can tick anything — a MonoBehaviour, a pooled projectile, a plain C# object — without each one paying for its own Unity Update callback.
whenToImplement: When there will be many of a thing and per-object Update cost is real: projectiles, crowd agents, swarm enemies. For a handful of objects, an ordinary Update is simpler and costs nothing worth measuring.

Tick(float).contract: One frame of behaviour. deltaTime is passed in rather than read, so the manager decides what time means — scaled, unscaled, or a fixed step.
Tick(float).mustNot: Do not read Time.deltaTime inside. Taking the passed value is what lets the manager change the clock for everything at once.

calledBy: UpdateManager, once per frame, in registration order. Nothing calls it otherwise — an unregistered ITickable simply never ticks, with no error.
useCases: Projectiles that tick from a pool without their own Update.
Crowd or swarm agents where the count makes per-object Update expensive.
Plain C# simulation objects with no GameObject at all.

gotchas.title: A MonoBehaviour implementing it still has its own Update
gotchas.body: Unity keeps calling Update independently. Put the per-frame work in Tick only, or it runs twice.
